## The Shore Seen from One Vessel

Love begins when the other is no longer merely an image inside me.

Before that, there may be attraction, pleasure, dependency, fantasy,
gratitude, hunger, fear, habit, or reward. These are real records. They
are not yet love. They are weather inside one history.

Another person is not the weather inside my history. Another person is
another history.

The difference is like a shoreline seen from one vessel. I can chart
the coast. I can remember its lights. I can mistake fog for cliffs or
paint a harbor where there is none. But the shore is not the chart in
my cabin. It answers with its own rock, tide, refusal, growth, silence,
and storm.

Love begins when the chart becomes corrigible by the shore.

```{=html}
<span class="elim-mark">✗ "Love is the intensity of my representation."</span>
```

No. Intensity can belong to projection. Love requires the other history
to be allowed to correct the representation.

## Against Projection

Projection is a closed room pretending to be a window. It uses the
other as a screen for old wounds, desired futures, unmet needs, or
private myths. The projected other may be adored, praised, pursued, or
protected. Yet the real other has been displaced.

In BEDC terms, projection treats $\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t)$ as if it
were $H_j(t)$. The representation becomes an idol. It refuses
correction by the other's actual response.

Love breaks that idol. It does not break tenderness. It breaks the
false identity:

$$
\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t)=H_j(t).
$$

The loved other remains partly unowned. That unowned remainder is not a
defect of love. It is the air love breathes.

## Against Possession

Possession wants the other history to become a stable resource. It
wants continuation, but only continuation under my control. It wants
the river to keep flowing, but only through my mill.

Love cannot be possession because love supports the positive
continuation of the other as other. It may make promises. It may create
shared forms, houses, language, rituals, projects, memories. But the
shared form is not allowed to erase the other history.

Intimacy is therefore not fusion. Two histories may stand close enough
to warm each other and still not become one history. The distance
between them is not coldness. It is the condition under which relation
can be honest.

## Care Is Not Substitution

Care is often confused with control because both can act. A controlling
hand and a caring hand may both reach toward the same wound. But one
hand closes over the path; the other steadies the path so the other can
walk.

In BEDC, care supports $\Cont^+$ of the other history under a value
horizon. The phrase "under recognition" matters. Without recognition,
care degrades into management. Without positive continuation,
recognition becomes passive witnessing.

Love is neither cold respect nor warm capture. It is a difficult middle
verb: to stand near another finite history and will its truthful
continuation without replacing it.

## Truth Fidelity

Love cannot be built out of systematic falsification. A lie may protect
a mood, a relationship-image, a social arrangement, or a fantasy of
peace. But it breaks the ledger on which love depends.

Truth fidelity does not mean saying every possible fact at every
moment. It means refusing to keep the relation alive by hiding the gap,
forging the promise, or editing the other history into convenience.

A bridge with a crack may still be crossed if the crack is known. A
bridge covered with flowers and declared whole has already betrayed the
traveler.

## The T-Value of the Other

Love also encounters a value that utility cannot exhaust. The loved
other may be useful, delightful, beautiful, difficult, costly, or
painful. None of those predicates settles the question:

why is this finite other worthy?

If the answer is only "because this other benefits me," love has
collapsed into exchange. If the answer is "because this other satisfies
my image," love has collapsed into projection. Love keeps a value
socket open. It treats the finite other as a point at which worth
exceeds the utility ledger.

This does not make the other infinite. It makes the finite other
inexhaustible by my accounting.

## Grief

Because love supports the other's positive continuation, love is
exposed to death. Grief is not a malfunction added to love from
outside. It is love reading the failure of embodied continuation while
fidelity remains.

The cup is broken; the water is not in this cup anymore. The table
still remembers the hand that lifted it. The room is changed not
because a private reward was lost, but because another history that
could answer, refuse, grow, and correct the world has reached its local
boundary.

Love gives mortality weight. Mortality gives love gravity.

## Strict Mathematical Form

Let $H_i(t),H_j(t)\in\Hist$ be focused histories at stage $t$. Let
$\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t)$ be $i$'s internal representation of $j$.

Define other-Hist recognition:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Recognize}_i(j,t)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\neg\hsame(H_i(t),H_j(t))\\
&{}\wedge
\neg\operatorname{Projection}_i(j,t)\\
&{}\wedge
\neg\operatorname{Objectify}_i(j,t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{CorrigibleBy}_{H_j}(\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t))\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{GapHonest}_i(H_j(t),\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $V_j$ be a value horizon for $j$. Define positive-continuation care:
$$
\operatorname{Care}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\operatorname{Policy}_i(t)
\text{ supports }
\Cont^+_{V_j}(H_j,t)
\text{ under }
\operatorname{Recognize}_i(j,t).
$$

Define truth fidelity:
$$
\operatorname{TruthFidelity}_{i\to j}(t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\neg\operatorname{RealityFalsification}_{i\to j}(t)
\wedge
\neg\operatorname{GapConcealment}_{i\to j}(t).
$$

Define T-oriented worth:
$$
\operatorname{TValue}_i(j,t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\operatorname{Worth}_i(j,t)
\not\equiv
f_i(\operatorname{Utility}_i(j,t)).
$$

Define love:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{Recognize}_i(j,t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{Care}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{TruthFidelity}_{i\to j}(t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{SelfTransform}_{i\leftarrow j}(t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{TValue}_i(j,t).
\end{aligned}
$$

Then:
$$
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\Rightarrow
\neg\operatorname{Projection}_i(j,t),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\Rightarrow
\neg\operatorname{Objectify}_i(j,t),
$$

and
$$
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Care}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t).
$$

Liking is a reward predicate:
$$
\operatorname{Like}_{i\to j}(t)
\Longleftrightarrow
\operatorname{Reward}_i(\operatorname{Rep}_i(j,t))>0.
$$

The non-collapse laws are:
$$
\operatorname{Like}_{i\to j}(t)
\not\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)
\not\Rightarrow
\operatorname{Like}_{i\to j}(t).
$$

Mutual love with shared meaning is:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{MutualLove}_{i,j}^{V_i,V_j}(t)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{Love}^{V_j}_{i\to j}(t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{Love}^{V_i}_{j\to i}(t)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{SharedMeaning}_{ij}(t).
\end{aligned}
$$

The strict summary is:
$$
\operatorname{Love}
=
\operatorname{OtherHistRecognition}
+
\operatorname{PositiveContinuationCare}
+
\operatorname{TruthFidelity}
+
\operatorname{TValue}.
$$
